issues.description: v3-beta default speaker disagrees between docstring/PR description and TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS
issues.detail: The module docstring, class docstring, and PR description state that the default speaker for bulbul:v3-beta is 'aditya', but TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS sets default_speaker='shubh'. This is a direct contradiction between the documented contract and the implementation. A caller relying on the documented default will get a different voice than promised. Pick one source of truth and make the other follow.

issues.description: Silent pace clamping is inconsistent with rest of validation policy
issues.detail: When pace is outside the model-specific range, the code warns and silently clamps to the nearest valid value, while other unsupported parameters (prompt, mode, model name) raise ValueError. The caller's specification ('synthesize at pace=X') is silently substituted with pace=clamp(X) with only a log line. Either reject with ValueError uniformly or accept and document the clamp as a feature — mixing the two creates incoherent contracts.

issues.description: Ignored-parameter warnings use float-equality against defaults to infer user intent
issues.detail: The checks `params.pitch != 0.0`, `params.loudness != 1.0`, `params.temperature != 0.6` conflate 'user explicitly set this' with 'value differs from default'. A user who explicitly passes pitch=0.0 to v3 gets no warning; a user who passes temperature=0.6 explicitly to v2 gets no warning. Use Optional[...] = None sentinels (or pydantic's model_fields_set) so warnings reflect user intent rather than value equality, and avoid float-equality fragility.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 speakers for unknown models
issues.detail: The function returns the v2 speaker list for any unknown model name rather than raising or returning an empty list. This contradicts the strict validation done in __init__ and lies to callers using the result to validate user input — they will accept v2 voices for an unknown model. Either raise on unknown models (matching the constructor's behavior) or return an empty list with a documented contract; silent fallback is a leaky abstraction.

issues.description: input_audio_codec silently dropped from STT connect_kwargs without explanation
issues.detail: The previous _connect built `input_audio_codec` into connect_kwargs; the new version drops it with no comment. self._input_audio_codec is still stored on the instance and exposed in __init__ but is no longer transmitted to the SDK. If intentional because v3 infers codec elsewhere, document it; if accidental, this is a regression for v2 callers. Either remove the parameter entirely, restore the kwarg, or add a one-line literate comment explaining the change.

issues.description: Capability flags are encoded as parallel booleans rather than a single set, duplicating validation logic
issues.detail: ModelConfig and TTSModelConfig fan out into many supports_X booleans (supports_prompt, supports_mode, supports_language, supports_pitch, supports_loudness, supports_temperature). Validation logic is then repeated at init, setters, and payload construction. A single `supported_params: frozenset[str]` per model would let validation become `name in cfg.supported_params` and payload construction become a filter — eliminating the need to touch multiple sites when Sarvam adds a parameter.

issues.description: voice_id is not validated against the model's speaker set at construction
issues.detail: Each model has a disjoint speaker set (V2 vs V3) encoded in SarvamTTSSpeakerV2/V3 enums and TTSModelConfig.speakers, yet __init__ accepts any string for voice_id without validating it against self._config.speakers. A caller can construct SarvamHttpTTSService(model='bulbul:v2', voice_id='aditya') and only fail at API-call time. Enforce membership at construction time and fail fast with the list of permitted speakers.

issues.description: Pydantic Field(ge=, le=) pace range contradicts per-model pace_range
issues.detail: InputParams declares pace with Field(ge=0.3, le=3.0) — a global precondition — while TTSModelConfig sets pace_range=(0.5, 2.0) for v3-beta. A v3-beta user passing pace=2.5 passes Pydantic validation, then gets silently clamped at construction. Two specifications for the same parameter produce an incoherent contract. Choose one enforcement layer.
issues.lines: InputParams pace field and clamping logic

issues.description: Speaker enums duplicate the data already in the config tuples
issues.detail: SarvamTTSSpeakerV2/V3 enums encode speaker names that are then re-encoded as `tuple(s.value for s in ...)` in TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS and again returned as a list by get_speakers_for_model. Three representations of the same data must be kept in sync. Either commit to the enums as the source of truth and validate against them, or drop the enums and keep a single frozenset per model.

issues.description: vad_signals and high_vad_sensitivity declared as `bool` with default None
issues.detail: InputParams declares `vad_signals: bool = None` and `high_vad_sensitivity: bool = None`. The annotated type is bool but the default is None — pydantic accepts this but the static type is wrong. Should be `Optional[bool] = None`. Pre-existing but adjacent to this PR and worth fixing while the file is open.

issues.description: MODEL_CONFIGS/TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS lack documented invariants and immutability
issues.detail: The dataclasses are frozen but the outer registries are plain Dict, and cross-field invariants (e.g. supports_mode True implies default_mode non-None; use_translate_endpoint co-varies with use_translate_method) are implicit rather than enforced. Type as Mapping or wrap in MappingProxyType to make the immutability invariant explicit, and consider validating cross-field invariants in __post_init__ so future additions cannot silently violate them.

issues.description: set_prompt silent no-op on non-supporting models weakens postcondition asymmetrically
issues.detail: set_prompt(None) on a model that does not support prompts silently returns, while set_prompt('x') raises. The postcondition 'prompt is cleared' is not preserved uniformly. Either explicitly document the asymmetric behavior or make it uniformly raise on non-supporting models. The current shape is a subtle LSP-style weakening callers cannot rely on.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor from string-sniffing (`'saaras' in model.lower()`) to a registry-based ModelConfig/TTSModelConfig is the right direction and lands the STT path on solid footing. The TTS half is less disciplined and ships several contract contradictions: the documented v3-beta default speaker ('aditya') disagrees with the configured value ('shubh'); pace is silently clamped while other unsupported parameters raise; Pydantic-level pace ranges contradict per-model ranges; 'ignored parameter' warnings use float-equality against defaults instead of detecting user intent; get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 for unknown models; and voice_id is never validated against the model's speaker set despite the new enums. The capability fan-out into parallel boolean flags (supports_prompt, supports_pitch, etc.) duplicates validation logic across init/setters/payload construction and would be better expressed as a single supported_params frozenset per model. The silent removal of input_audio_codec from STT connect_kwargs is a behavior change that needs explanation or reversal. Fix the contract contradictions and pick one enforcement layer per parameter; the structural cleanups (collapse booleans to a set, dedupe enums vs tuples) are taste improvements that pay back on the next model addition.
